title: Recipe 11 — Managed Multitenant (one daemon, many tenants, no shared storage)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Recipe 11 is the SaaS shape: one deployment, many customers, and isolation you can prove rather than promise.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the gateway needs a Claude credential to actually answer a run.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape, add the shared agent
beats.cue: “target: managed — a long-running gateway daemon. And one agent block, shared by every tenant.”

beats.label: Declare tenant-a and its budget
beats.cue: “A tenant is an id plus a token budget — and the budget is a first-class spec field, not external policy.”

beats.label: Declare tenant-b
beats.cue: “Second tenant: same agent, its own budget, its own storage tree, its own audit chain.”

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The tenants array survives lowering — ids and budgets, exactly as written. The gateway reads this, not the YAML.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target managed, tenants included

beats.label: Compile the daemon — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots the daemon: GREEN, no key. A gateway that can't answer is still a gateway that came up.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (7 anchors); install ok; boot ok (daemon stayed alive for the liveness window)

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: “JWT verify, tenant rebase, budget gate, audit chain — 351 lines of TypeScript you own outright.”

beats.label: Hand it a weak signing secret
beats.cue: “Under sixteen characters and it refuses to start rather than serving tenants on a guessable secret. Exit 1, on purpose.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — daemon.ts line 23 checks the length before it binds: “CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET is set but too short (min 16 chars). Refusing to start.” then process.exit(1). Set inline so it does not leak into the beats after it

beats.label: Pin the JWT secret
beats.cue: “Now a real one — at least sixteen chars — pinned so tokens survive a restart.”

verify.note: without this the daemon generates a one-shot dev secret and prints it on stderr

beats.label: Put tenant storage under live/
beats.cue: CREWHAUS_TENANTS_ROOT — line 20 of the daemon we just opened. Keeps the audit log on camera instead of in /tmp.

verify.note: default is /tmp/crewhaus-tenants; rebasing keeps the take self-contained

beats.label: Boot the gateway
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Gateway listening on :3000.” Backgrounded, so this same terminal can drive it.

verify.note: the daemon binds with no key; serving a run needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Mint a token for tenant-a
beats.cue: “JWT issuance is out of scope for the gateway — it only verifies.” Here that's local HS256 over the secret we just pinned.
beats.command: TENANT_A_JWT=$(bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { signJwt } from "@crewhaus/gateway-server"; console.log(signJwt({ tenant_id: "tenant-a" }, process.env.CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET))')

verify.note: keyless — signing is local HS256 over the secret run-secret exported into this same terminal; also proves @crewhaus/gateway-server resolves from the checked bundle

beats.label: Start a run as tenant-a
beats.cue: [needs-key] “JWT in, JSON-RPC out, audit log written.” One authenticated call and runs.create comes back with a runId.
beats.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_A_JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"protocol":"crewhaus.v1","id":"1","method":"runs.create","params":{"spec":"hello-managed","input":"What is the capital of France?","sessionId":"sess_0123456789abcdef"}}'

verify.note: the crewhaus.v1 envelope, not the bare jsonrpc-2.0 one the recipe prints. sessionId is passed explicitly because the managed codegen's default id is rejected by session-store (it wants sess_<16 hex>). Keyless it answers internal_error: no Anthropic credentials

groups.title: One more thing · the invariant target: managed exists to enforce

beats.label: Read tenant-a's audit chain
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Every event carries the SHA-256 of the prior event.” GENESIS, then hash, then hash — tampering is detectable, which is the property an auditor cares about.

verify.note: written by run-create: gateway_request (prevHash GENESIS), policy_decision, model_call — each chained to the previous record's hash

beats.label: Mint a token for tenant-b
beats.cue: Same daemon, same secret, a different tenant_id claim — and again no key involved.
beats.command: TENANT_B_JWT=$(bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { signJwt } from "@crewhaus/gateway-server"; console.log(signJwt({ tenant_id: "tenant-b" }, process.env.CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET))')

verify.note: keyless, like run-mint; tenant-b is the second id declared in the spec's tenants: block

beats.label: Start a run as tenant-b
beats.cue: [needs-key] Same endpoint, second tenant — the gateway rebases every storage path on the claim it just verified.
beats.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_B_JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"protocol":"crewhaus.v1","id":"2","method":"runs.create","params":{"spec":"hello-managed","input":"What is the capital of Japan?","sessionId":"sess_fedcba9876543210"}}'

verify.note: creates live/tenants/tenant-b/ on the first authenticated call; same sessionId caveat as run-create

beats.label: Show the two tenant trees
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Cross-tenant reads are impossible by construction.” Two roots, no shared directory — that's the whole claim, on disk.

verify.note: after both runs: tenant-a and tenant-b, each with its own audit/, sessions/ and state/ subtree

beats.label: Stop the gateway
beats.cue: [needs-key] Take's over — kill the backgrounded daemon before it holds :3000 forever.

verify.note: job %1 is the daemon run-boot backgrounded into this same terminal
